quick_english: Arjuna asks which devotees are most accomplished in yoga, those who worship the Lord or those who worship the unmanifest.
cite_parts: atha dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate
evam-uktena nayena ye seśvarabrahmopāsakāḥ ye ca  kevalamātmamātra-mupāsate teṣāṃ viśeṣākhyānāya praśnaḥ

quick_english: The Lord declares that devotees who enter him with mind and worship him with supreme faith are most united.
cite_parts: śrībhagavānuvāca   mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate
māheśvaryaviṣayo yeṣāṃ samāveśaḥ-akṛtrimastanmayībhāvaḥ te  yuktatamā mama matāḥ-ityanena pratijñā kriyate

quick_english: Those who worship the imperishable, indescribable, unmanifest, all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, and firm.
By restraining the senses and being equal-minded everywhere, devoted to all beings' welfare, they attain me alone.
The unmanifest path is hard for embodied beings; even Brahman-worshippers attain the Lord, but with greater effort.
cite_parts: ye punarakṣaraṃ brahmopāsate ātmānaṃ  sarvatragam-ityādibhirviśeṣaṇairātmanaḥ sarve īśvaradharmā  āropyante
ato brahmopāsakā api māmeva yadyapi yānti  tathāpyadhikatarasteṣāṃ kleśaḥ
ātmani  kilāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇāṣṭakāropaṃ vidhāya  paścāttamevopāsate iti svataḥsiddhaguṇagrāmagarimaṇi  īśvare'yatnasādhye sthite'pi dviguṇamāyāsaṃ vindanti

quick_english: Those who renounce all actions into me, devoted to me, meditate on me through yoga and worship.
cite_parts: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ

quick_english: For those whose minds are fixed in me, I, O Partha, become the deliverer from the ocean of death and samsara, and not after a long time.

quick_english: Place your mind in me alone and fix your intellect in me; you will dwell in me, abiding in supreme yoga. Those who renounce everything in me through the previously stated teaching are rescued by me from all obstacles and afflictions. The entering of mind is explained. This yoga is supreme because it is unartificial. When knowledge is awakened through the manifestation of distinguished means, posture, abiding, and samadhi possibility in my hymn, that is not your ever-flowing innate consciousness; because of the triad's presence, consciousness is clearly perceived here too. But when fuel-less, taking self-mastery and indifference to the body, consciousness suddenly knows itself and the fire of knowledge arises at once. Then, goddess, free from the supports of that body-person, one knows the great lord, who agitates the bonds of the powerless, and so forth.

quick_english: You cannot make the mind enter steadily into me by practice-yoga alone; then, O Dhanañjaya, to obtain me, without intense descent of divine power and long-pleased guru foot grace, absorption is difficult—thus practice.

quick_english: Even if you cannot practice, be devoted to right action; by performing actions for my sake you will attain perfection. Since practice is hindered by obstacles, therefore perform actions, worship, recitation, study, sacrifice, and the like to destroy them.

quick_english: Even if you are established in my yoga but unable to do this, renounce the fruits of all actions and remain self-controlled. If, from ignorance, you cannot perform divine action, then renounce all of it to me through self-offering, according to the method stated in scripture. Relying on that intent, I have spoken in an easy procedure. Whatever is deficient, excessive, unknown, lacking sequence, lacking attention, or a slip of intellect, forgive mercifully, O Shambhu, since you are full of compassion. By this yoga of hymn I offer your self; again, causelessly, I attain fitness for sufferings. In the supreme lordly doctrinal scriptures, this very intent is that of self-offering; this meaning is summarized.
cite_parts: yadi ca bhagavatkarma kartuṃ na śakto'si-ajñatvāt  śāstroktakramāvedanāt

quick_english: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation surpasses knowledge; from meditation comes renunciation of fruits and then peace. Since knowledge is absorption and practice's fruit is absorption, meditation as divine fullness is distinguished and attains desired realization; then action-fruits can be renounced, otherwise renunciation is nowhere; ultimate peace follows renunciation. Therefore absorption-natured knowledge, root of all, is principal.

quick_english: The devotee who does not hate any being, is friendly and compassionate, free of mine-ness and ego, equal in pain and joy, and forgiving is dear to the Lord.
cite_parts: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca
mamāmī-ityādiḥ  mamakāraḥ ahamudāro'haṃ tejasvī ahaṃ sahanaḥ-ityādiḥ  ahaṃkāraḥ-etau yasya na staḥ

quick_english: The yogi who is always content, self-controlled, firmly resolved, and has offered mind and intellect to the Lord is dear to the Lord.
He who does not agitate the world, is not agitated by it, and is freed from joy, anger, fear, and agitation is dear to the Lord.
cite_parts: harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ

quick_english: The devotee who expects nothing, is pure and skillful, remains indifferent, is free from pain, and renounces the fruits of all undertakings is dear to the Lord.
cite_parts: sarvārambhaphalatyāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

quick_english: He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, and renounces the fruits of good and bad is dear to the Lord.
cite_parts: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati

quick_english: Equal toward enemy and friend, in honor and dishonor, in cold, heat, pleasure, and pain, and free from attachment.
cite_parts: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāvamānayoḥ

quick_english: One who is equal in blame and praise, silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded, and devoted is dear to me.

tokens.grounds: compound describing one who remains even amid praise and blame

quick_english: Those who faithfully practice this immortal dharma are exceedingly dear; one without fixed resolve, accepting what comes and absorbed in the supreme Lord, easily attains supreme isolation.

yathāprāptahevākitayā sukhaduḥkhādikamupabhujjānaḥ  parameśvaraviṣayasamāveśitahṛdayaḥ sukhenaiva prāpnoti  paramakaivalyamiti śivam

label: 12-sangraha
quick_english: Here is the summary verse: the wealth of absorption born from supreme bliss is itself Brahman-being in all states, attained without effort.
